notes: OFF-THESIS FLAG: this is an oil/gas pipeline, not an AI/power/datacenter asset - included because it is a rare three-way consortium of watchlist names (Blackstone, Brookfield, KKR) on one of the largest infra deals of the window; tagged power-energy only as the closest available canonical slug, downstream should down-weight or exclude for AI-buildout purposes. Kuwait Petroleum Corp's unit Kuwait Oil Company (KOC) signed a 20.5-year lease-and-leaseback JV over its ~320km / 13-pipeline crude network (Project Peregrine). Consortium (Blackstone + Brookfield + KKR) takes a combined 49% non-controlling stake; KOC retains 51% plus full operational control. Deal generates ~$7.85bn of UPFRONT proceeds for Kuwait against a stated $16.0bn total partnership value; volume-based tariff, not oil-price-linked. Largest FDI in Kuwait's history. Per-firm split NOT disclosed in the Blackstone/KKR/Brookfield releases or wire coverage (CNBC, Bloomberg, The National, Rigzone, Energy Connects all report only the consortium totals) - secondary calculation implies an even ~1/3 of the 49% (~16.3% each) but this is unofficial, so amount_usd and ownership_pct are left blank on all three consortium rows to avoid a false-precision triple count; round_total_usd carries the $16.0bn deal total once. KKR's own Q2 2026 earnings release (Jul 30) separately confirms the deal as a named Q2/Q3 infrastructure highlight.
